# Alloq

Ressourcen- und Kapazitätsplanung für Softwareteams. Dieses Design System ist aus dem Code der Anwendung abgeleitet: `assets/css/alloq-theme.css`, `app/styles.py`, das Mantine-Theme in `app/app.py` und die Komponenten unter `components/` und `app/components/`. Die UI läuft auf Reflex mit Mantine (`appkit_mantine`). Das Theme legt die eigenen `--alloq-*` Variablen und umgefärbte Mantine-Paletten über die Standardwerte.

## Content Fundamentals

- **Sprache:** Deutsch, sachlich, kurze Wörter. Navigation, Buttons, Status und Meldungen sind deutsch: „Ressourcenplanung“, „Projekt anlegen“, „Abbrechen“, „Keine offenen Risiken.“
- **Titel:** kurze Substantive („Feiertage“, „Projekt Details“). Darüber ein Breadcrumb, darunter höchstens ein Satz Beschreibung.
- **Buttons:** Verb oder Verb mit Objekt. Die Hauptaktion eines Modals nennt das Objekt: „Projekt speichern“.
- **Kennzahlen:** Labels in Versalien („AUSLASTUNG“, „PT FREI“), die Zahl ist die Aussage.
- **Zahlen und Daten:** deutsches Format. Beträge „480.000 €“, kurz „1,2M €“ oder „850T €“. Daten „TT.MM.JJJJ“ oder „1. Sep 2026“. Kalenderwochen „KW 42“. Personentage „PT“.
- **Leere Zustände** sagen, was fehlt, mit Punkt am Ende.
- Keine Ausrufezeichen, keine Emojis.

## Visual Foundations

- **Ton:** warm und ruhig. Ein cremeweißer Grund (`bg-base`) trägt einen weichen Verlauf aus Gold, Salbeigrün, Lavendel und Teal. Im dunklen Modus wird der Grund zu tiefem Petrol (`#141e21`) mit dunklen Blau-, Grün- und Violetttönen.
- **Farbe:** Die Mantine-Primärpalette ist `alloqTeal` (Stufe 6 hell, 7 dunkel). Teal ist die Handlungsfarbe (`primary-filled`, `nav-active-bg`). Gold (`warm-*`, Palette `alloqWarm`) ist die Markenfarbe für Flächen und die Radix-Akzente, nie für kleinen Text. Salbei, Gelb, Terrakotta und Rot tragen Status. Alle Mantine-Paletten außer Violett sind auf diese gedämpften Töne umgefärbt.
- **Flächen:** Karten sind halbtransparent (`fade-bg`, `surface`) und lassen den Verlauf durchscheinen. Modale, Drawer, Tabellenköpfe und das Planungsraster sind deckend (`surface-muted`, `surface-solid`).
- **Rahmen statt Schatten:** Linien in blassem Grün (`border`). Schatten nur für schwebende Elemente (`shadow-soft`), Formularabschnitte und die Modal-Fußzeile.
- **Radien:** `radius-sm` für Tabellen, Raster und Balken, `radius-md` für Eingaben und Buttons, `radius-lg` für Karten, Modale und Drawer, `radius-xl` für Badges und Fortschrittsbalken.
- **Typografie:** Roboto Flex für alles, Roboto Mono für Code, Major Mono Display nur für das Wortzeichen. Seitentitel sind sehr leicht (280, 3rem), Kennzahlen kräftig (700), Namen in Karten 800.
- **Daten:** Tabellenziffern in Rastern und Tabellen. Die aktuelle Woche ist golden hinterlegt (`current-week`).
- **Bewegung:** nur Hintergrundübergänge von 120 bis 200ms bei Hover und ein Skelett-Schimmer beim Laden.

## Iconography

Lucide über `rx.icon`, Strichstärke 1.5px (gesetzt in `base_style`). Größen: 20px in Buttons der Größe `md` und in der Navigation, 16px in Feldern und Kartentiteln, 14px in kleinen Aktionen, 48px in leeren Zuständen. Icons tragen die Textfarbe ihrer Umgebung. Icon-Schaltflächen haben immer ein `aria-label` und einen Tooltip. Die Vorschauen laden die genutzten Lucide-Pfade aus `icons/lucide.js` (aus `lucide-react` 1.26.0).

## Usage Rules

1. Text in `text` oder `text-muted` auf `bg-base`, `surface`, `surface-muted` oder `fade-bg`. `text-muted` nicht unter 11px.
2. Pro Ansicht ein gefüllter Button (`primary-filled` mit `nav-active-text`). Gold ist keine Buttonfarbe: weißer Text erreicht darauf nur 1.8:1.
3. Status immer als Paar aus Grund und Text: Badge-Grund `*-light`, Text `*-7` (dunkel `*-3`). Das Wort steht immer im Badge.
4. Auslastung nutzt die `heat-*` Stufen, Wochensummen die `cap-*` Stufen, Risiken die `risk-*` Skala. Die Zahl steht immer in der Zelle.
5. Diagrammreihen nutzen die `chart-*` Tokens. Prognosen sind gestrichelt.
6. Löschen nur mit Bestätigungsdialog.
7. Seiteninhalt höchstens `content-max-width` breit. Die Planungsansichten füllen den Platz zwischen Navigation und rechtem Rand.
8. Neue Farben zuerst als Token in `alloq-theme.css` anlegen, hell und dunkel zusammen.

## Komponenten

Die Komponentenseiten zeigen statische Nachbauten in HTML und CSS. Die Stile stehen in `components/bundle.css` (Klassen `aq-*`) und nutzen nur Tokens.

| Gruppe | Komponenten |
| --- | --- |
| Actions | Button, ActionIcon |
| Inputs | TextInput, Select, Switch |
| Navigation | Navigation, SegmentedControl, ViewModeToggle, Tabs |
| Layout | PageHeader, Toolbar, FilterRow, FormSection |
| Data display | Badge, Avatar, Progress, DataTable |
| Cards | ProjectCard, EmployeeCard |
| Dashboard | KpiCard, CapacityCard, RiskList, ForecastChart |
| Planning | PlanningGrid, Heatmap, Gantt, RiskMatrix |
| Overlays | ModalDrawer, ConfirmDialog, UserMenu, Tooltip |
| Feedback | EmptyState |

## Not synced

- Der Seitenverlauf `--alloq-app-bg` besteht aus fünf Radialverläufen und lässt sich nicht als Token abbilden. Er steht in `assets/css/alloq-theme.css`.
- Die Radix-Variablen (`--accent-*`, `--blue-*` usw.) und die vollständigen Mantine-Skalen 0 bis 9 sind nur teilweise als Tokens übernommen.
- Die Reflex-Komponenten selbst sind nicht gebündelt. Die Vorschauen sind Nachbauten.
- Violett (`cap-tight`, Prognosen) und Blau 0 bis 1 (`cap-absent`) sind Mantine-Standardfarben und passen nicht zur gedämpften Palette.
- Einige Texte sind noch englisch („Search by name“, „Planned Value“).
- `assets/img/logo.svg` enthält ein fremdes Wortzeichen (Voyager) und wurde nicht übernommen.

"""Planning Heatmap view: pill-style cells with usage percent + colors."""

from __future__ import annotations

import reflex as rx
from alloq_commons.components.formatters import match_str
from alloq_project.components.planning_shared import (
    GRID_WRAPPER_STYLE,
    LABEL_COL_WIDTH,
    grid_row,
)
from alloq_project.states.planning_grid_state import (
    EmployeeBlock,
    HeatCell,
    MonthSpan,
    PlanningStore,
    WeekColumn,
)
from reflex.vars import ObjectVar

import appkit_mantine as mn

HEAT_ROW_HEIGHT = "56px"
HEAT_HEADER_BG = "var(--alloq-surface-muted)"
HEAT_FOOTER_BG = "var(--alloq-surface-muted)"

ABSENT_STRIPE_BG = (
    "repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, "
    "light-dark(rgba(0,0,0,0.04), rgba(255,255,255,0.05)), "
    "light-dark(rgba(0,0,0,0.04), rgba(255,255,255,0.05)) 4px, "
    "light-dark(rgba(0,0,0,0.10), rgba(255,255,255,0.12)) 4px, "
    "light-dark(rgba(0,0,0,0.10), rgba(255,255,255,0.12)) 8px)"
)


def _heat_bg(bucket: rx.Var[str]) -> rx.Var[str]:
    return match_str(
        bucket,
        ("low", "light-dark(var(--mantine-color-red-1), rgba(250,82,82,0.20))"),
        ("mid", "light-dark(var(--mantine-color-yellow-2), rgba(250,176,5,0.30))"),
        (
            "high",
            "light-dark(var(--mantine-color-green-2), var(--mantine-color-green-6))",
        ),
        # Overbooked is a warning, not the best state (matches the grid's red).
        (
            "over",
            "light-dark(var(--mantine-color-red-4), var(--mantine-color-red-8))",
        ),
        ("absent", ABSENT_STRIPE_BG),
        "transparent",
    )


def _heat_fg(bucket: rx.Var[str]) -> rx.Var[str]:
    return match_str(
        bucket,
        (
            "low",
            "light-dark(var(--mantine-color-red-9), var(--mantine-color-red-3))",
        ),
        (
            "mid",
            "light-dark(var(--mantine-color-yellow-9), var(--mantine-color-yellow-2))",
        ),
        (
            "high",
            "light-dark(var(--mantine-color-green-9), var(--mantine-color-green-3))",
        ),
        (
            "over",
            "light-dark(var(--mantine-color-red-9), var(--mantine-color-red-0))",
        ),
        (
            "absent",
            "light-dark(var(--mantine-color-gray-7), var(--mantine-color-gray-4))",
        ),
        "var(--alloq-text)",
    )


# ---------------------------- Header ---------------------------------------


def _heatmap_label_th(text: str) -> rx.Component:
    return mn.box(
        mn.text(
            text,
            size="xs",
            fw="700",
            c="var(--alloq-text-muted)",
            style={"letterSpacing": "0.06em", "textTransform": "uppercase"},
        ),
        style={
            "position": "sticky",
            "left": "0",
            "zIndex": "40",
            "backgroundColor": HEAT_HEADER_BG,
            "padding": "8px 16px",
            "minWidth": LABEL_COL_WIDTH,
            "width": LABEL_COL_WIDTH,
            "display": "flex",
            "alignItems": "center",
            "borderRight": "1px solid var(--alloq-border)",
            "borderBottom": "1px solid var(--alloq-border)",
        },
    )


def _month_cell(month: ObjectVar[MonthSpan]) -> rx.Component:
    return mn.box(
        mn.text(month.label, size="sm", fw="600", c="var(--alloq-text)"),
        style={
            "gridColumn": "span " + month.span.to_string(),
            "backgroundColor": HEAT_HEADER_BG,
            "padding": "10px 8px",
            "display": "flex",
            "alignItems": "center",
            "borderBottom": "1px solid var(--alloq-border)",
        },
    )


def _week_no_cell(week: ObjectVar[WeekColumn]) -> rx.Component:
    return mn.box(
        mn.text(
            week.week_no.to_string(),
            size="xs",
            c="var(--alloq-text-muted)",
            fw="500",
        ),
        style={
            "backgroundColor": HEAT_HEADER_BG,
            "padding": "6px 0 8px",
            "display": "flex",
            "alignItems": "center",
            "justifyContent": "center",
            "borderBottom": "1px solid var(--alloq-border)",
        },
    )


def _heatmap_header() -> rx.Component:
    return mn.box(
        grid_row(
            _heatmap_label_th("Mitarbeiter"),
            rx.foreach(PlanningStore.month_spans, _month_cell),
        ),
        grid_row(
            mn.box(
                style={
                    "position": "sticky",
                    "left": "0",
                    "zIndex": "40",
                    "backgroundColor": HEAT_HEADER_BG,
                    "minWidth": LABEL_COL_WIDTH,
                    "width": LABEL_COL_WIDTH,
                    "borderRight": "1px solid var(--alloq-border)",
                    "borderBottom": "1px solid var(--alloq-border)",
                },
            ),
            rx.foreach(PlanningStore.weeks, _week_no_cell),
        ),
        style={
            "position": "sticky",
            "top": "0",
            "zIndex": "30",
            "backgroundColor": HEAT_HEADER_BG,
        },
    )


# ---------------------------- Body -----------------------------------------


def _heat_pill(cell: ObjectVar[HeatCell]) -> rx.Component:
    inner = rx.cond(
        cell.is_absent,
        rx.icon("plane", size=16, color="var(--alloq-text-muted)"),
        mn.text(
            cell.percent.to_string(),
            size="sm",
            fw="600",
            c=_heat_fg(cell.bucket),
        ),
    )
    return mn.box(
        mn.box(
            inner,
            style={
                "background": _heat_bg(cell.bucket),
                "borderRadius": "6px",
                "minHeight": "36px",
                "display": "flex",
                "alignItems": "center",
                "justifyContent": "center",
                "width": "100%",
            },
        ),
        style={
            "padding": "6px 4px",
            "display": "flex",
            "alignItems": "center",
            "justifyContent": "center",
            "minHeight": HEAT_ROW_HEIGHT,
        },
    )


def _employee_label_cell(emp: ObjectVar[EmployeeBlock]) -> rx.Component:
    return mn.box(
        mn.group(
            mn.avatar(
                name=emp.name,
                color="var(--alloq-accent-strong)",
                size="md",
                radius="xl",
            ),
            mn.stack(
                mn.text(
                    emp.name,
                    size="sm",
                    fw="700",
                    c="var(--alloq-text)",
                    lh="1.15",
                ),
                rx.cond(
                    emp.job_title != "",
                    mn.text(
                        emp.job_title,
                        size="xs",
                        c="var(--alloq-text-muted)",
                    ),
                    rx.fragment(),
                ),
                gap="2px",
            ),
            gap="sm",
            align="center",
            wrap="nowrap",
        ),
        style={
            "position": "sticky",
            "left": "0",
            "zIndex": "2",
            "backgroundColor": "var(--alloq-surface-solid)",
            "padding": "0 16px",
            "minWidth": LABEL_COL_WIDTH,
            "width": LABEL_COL_WIDTH,
            "minHeight": HEAT_ROW_HEIGHT,
            "display": "flex",
            "alignItems": "center",
            "borderBottom": "1px solid var(--alloq-border)",
            "borderRight": "1px solid var(--alloq-border)",
        },
    )


def _heat_row(emp: ObjectVar[EmployeeBlock]) -> rx.Component:
    return grid_row(
        _employee_label_cell(emp),
        rx.foreach(emp.heat, _heat_pill),
        style={
            "minHeight": HEAT_ROW_HEIGHT,
            "_hover": {"backgroundColor": "var(--alloq-surface-hover)"},
        },
    )


# ---------------------------- Footer ---------------------------------------


def _avg_footer_cell(cell: ObjectVar[HeatCell]) -> rx.Component:
    return mn.box(
        mn.box(
            mn.text(
                cell.percent.to_string(),
                size="xs",
                fw="700",
                c=_heat_fg(cell.bucket),
            ),
            style={
                "background": _heat_bg(cell.bucket),
                "borderRadius": "6px",
                "minHeight": "32px",
                "display": "flex",
                "alignItems": "center",
                "justifyContent": "center",
                "width": "100%",
            },
        ),
        style={
            "padding": "4px 4px",
            "display": "flex",
            "alignItems": "center",
            "justifyContent": "center",
            "minHeight": HEAT_ROW_HEIGHT,
        },
    )


def _heatmap_footer() -> rx.Component:
    return grid_row(
        mn.box(
            mn.text(
                "Durchschnitt Ø",
                size="xs",
                fw="700",
                c="var(--alloq-text-muted)",
                style={"letterSpacing": "0.06em", "textTransform": "uppercase"},
            ),
            style={
                "position": "sticky",
                "left": "0",
                "zIndex": "40",
                "backgroundColor": HEAT_FOOTER_BG,
                "padding": "8px 16px",
                "minWidth": LABEL_COL_WIDTH,
                "width": LABEL_COL_WIDTH,
                "minHeight": HEAT_ROW_HEIGHT,
                "display": "flex",
                "alignItems": "center",
                "borderRight": "1px solid var(--alloq-border)",
            },
        ),
        rx.foreach(PlanningStore.avg_heat, _avg_footer_cell),
        style={
            "position": "sticky",
            "bottom": "0",
            "zIndex": "20",
            "backgroundColor": HEAT_FOOTER_BG,
            "borderTop": "1px solid var(--alloq-border)",
            "borderBottom": "1px solid var(--alloq-border)",
        },
    )


def planning_heatmap() -> rx.Component:
    return rx.cond(
        PlanningStore.is_loaded,
        mn.box(
            _heatmap_header(),
            mn.box(
                rx.foreach(PlanningStore.employees, _heat_row),
            ),
            _heatmap_footer(),
            id="planning-heatmap-root",
            style={**GRID_WRAPPER_STYLE, "outline": "none"},
        ),
        mn.center(
            rx.hstack(
                rx.spinner(size="3"),
                mn.text("Lade Heatmap...", size="sm"),
                align="center",
                spacing="3",
            ),
            py="xl",
        ),
    )

content.text:
I made the redesign as a Claude Design canvas with the Alloq design system: **[Heatmap Redesign](https://claude.ai/artifact/RErjenmj7jDSRnQ2oSD3pX)**. It uses the same test data as your screenshot. I added one partial absence for Sandra so that state shows up. I haven't rendered or checked it in the browser.

**What I changed and why:**

1. **New color scale, so red means one thing.** Right now both 0 % and 222 % show as dark red, so most of the view looks like an alarm, especially weeks that just aren't planned yet. In the proposal, 0 to 100 % goes from an empty cell to solid teal, and the cells get stronger as more is booked. Only overbooking uses warm colors: clay for 101 to 150 % and dark red above 150 %. The steps also differ in lightness, not just color, so they're easier to tell apart for people with color blindness.
2. **Smaller cells.** The pills are about 26 px tall instead of 56 px, so all 26 weeks (6 months) fit on screen without scrolling sideways. A "comfortable" density setting is available in Tweaks.
3. **The current week is marked.** KW 42 has a gold column and a gold pill in the header. This uses the existing `current-week` token. The step from 2026 to 2027 gets a divider line.
4. **A legend** shows what each color range means, including full and partial absence. Partial absence is a small corner notch on the cell, so the number stays readable. Today it doesn't show at all.
5. **Two new sortable columns:** "Ø %" (average over the period) and "Frei ab" (first week with at least 30 % free). Together they answer "who is free, and when?" without scanning the rows. Clicking a column header sorts by it.
6. **Summary numbers at the top:** who is overbooked this week, free person-days (PT) this week, team utilization over the 6 months, and the next absence.
7. **Better footer.** It shows team utilization per week, weighted by capacity, plus a new **"PT frei"** row with free person-days per week. That number is easier to act on than an average.
8. **Details on click.** Clicking a cell opens a panel with the dates, booked vs. available PT, a capacity bar showing the overbooked part, the assignments for that week, and actions.
9. **Small fixes:** the cut-off switch label is shorter ("Interne Projekte ausblenden"), and "Nur verfügbare" became "Nur mit freier Kapazität" and works in the mockup.

Sorting, the filter switch and cell selection all work on the canvas. Dark mode and density are in Tweaks.

**Assumptions:** the project names in the details panel ("Projekt A" and so on) are placeholders. "Frei ab" uses the existing 70 % threshold. The canvas link is private until you share it from its Share menu.

"""Display settings of the planning grids; mixed into `PlanningStore`."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

import reflex as rx
from alloq_project.states.planning_models import (
    COMPACT_WEEK_COL_PX,
    LABEL_COL_PX,

)

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from alloq_project.states.planning_models import WeekColumn

NORMAL = "normal"
COMPACT = "kompakt"


class PlanningDisplayState(rx.State, mixin=True):
    """Row density and column layout of the planning grids.

    A mixin rather than a substate: the grid components read these vars next to
    `PlanningStore` vars, and the density must survive reloads per browser.
    """

    if TYPE_CHECKING:  # Provided by PlanningStore.
        weeks: list[WeekColumn]

    grid_density: str = rx.LocalStorage(NORMAL, name="alloq_planning_density")

    @rx.event
    def toggle_grid_density(self) -> None:
        self.grid_density = NORMAL if self.grid_density == COMPACT else COMPACT

    @rx.var(cache=True)
    def is_compact(self) -> bool:
        return self.grid_density == COMPACT

    @rx.var(cache=True)
    def week_col_px(self) -> int:
        return COMPACT_WEEK_COL_PX if self.grid_density == COMPACT else WEEK_COL_PX

    @rx.var(cache=True)

        return f"{LABEL_COL_PX + len(self.weeks) * self.week_col_px}px"

    @rx.var(cache=True)
    def grid_template_columns(self) -> str:
        return f"{LABEL_COL_PX}px repeat({len(self.weeks)}, {self.week_col_px}px)"

    @rx.var(cache=True)
    def month_start_keys(self) -> list[str]:
        return [w.key for w in self.weeks if w.is_month_start]

"""Single source of truth for planning data and views.

Allocations live once in `cells` keyed canonically by
``"{employee_id}|{project_code}|{week_key}"``. The two pivots — employee
blocks (Grid view) and project blocks (Project view) — are computed views of
the same store. Selection, navigation and in-cell editing run client-side in
the ``GridController`` component, which sends committed batches to
``apply_cell_changes``; dirtiness is tracked against the last loaded/saved
snapshot.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as dt
import logging
from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator

    def _filter_employees(self, blocks: list[EmployeeBlock]) -> list[EmployeeBlock]:
        """Apply scope, selection and remaining-capacity filters."""
        result = blocks
        if self.project_scope:
            own = owned_project_ids(self.all_projects, self.current_employee_id)
            result = [e for e in result if any(p.project_id in own for p in e.projects)]
        if self.employee_scope:
            mine = managed_employee_ids(
                self.available_employees, self.current_employee_id
            )
            result = [e for e in result if str(e.real_id) in mine]
        if self.project_filter:
            result = [
                e
                for e in result
                if any(p.project_id in self.project_filter for p in e.projects)
            ]
        if self.role_filter:
            result = [
                e
                for e in result
                if any(str(rid) in self.role_filter for rid in e.role_ids)
            ]
        if self.employee_filter:
            result = [e for e in result if str(e.real_id) in self.employee_filter]
        if self.available_only:
            result = [e for e in result if e.available_days > MIN_AVAILABLE_PT]
        return result

def dirty_keys_for(cells: dict[str, float], saved: dict[str, float]) -> list[str]:
    """Keys whose current value differs from the last loaded/saved snapshot."""
    return sorted(key for key, value in cells.items() if value != saved.get(key, 0.0))


def scaled_work_days(week: WeekColumn, workload_percent: int) -> float:
    """Apply workload percentage to a week's holiday-adjusted work days."""
    return UtilizationService.apply_workload(week.work_days, workload_percent)


def mark_repeats(cells: list[GridCell]) -> list[GridCell]:
    """Flag non-zero cells that repeat the previous week's value."""
    previous = 0.0
    for cell in cells:
        value = round(cell.value, FREE_DAYS_PRECISION)
        cell.is_repeat = value > 0 and value == previous
        previous = value
    return cells


def mark_defaults(cells: list[GridCell], default: float) -> list[GridCell]:
    """Flag cells holding the usual value so only deviations are shown."""
    usual = round(default, FREE_DAYS_PRECISION)
    for cell in cells:
        cell.is_default = round(cell.value, FREE_DAYS_PRECISION) == usual
    return cells


def gesamt_state(free_days: float) -> str:
    """Visual state of a Gesamt cell: overbooked, fully booked or free."""
    free_days = round(free_days, FREE_DAYS_PRECISION)
    if free_days < 0:
        return "over"
    if free_days == 0:
        return "zero"
    return "free"


MINUS = "\N{MINUS SIGN}"


def _de(value: float, *, signed: bool = False) -> str:
    text = f"{abs(value):.2f}".replace(".", ",")
    return f"{MINUS}{text}" if signed and value < 0 else text


def gesamt_breakdown(
    work: float, used: float, internal: float, absence: float, free: float
) -> str:
    """Tooltip text explaining how a week's free days are computed."""
    return (
        f"Arbeitstage {_de(work)} {MINUS} Projekte {_de(used)}"
        f" {MINUS} Intern {_de(internal)} {MINUS} Abwesenheit {_de(absence)}"
        f" = {_de(free, signed=True)} PT frei"
    )


def compute_gesamt(weeks: list[WeekColumn], block: EmployeeBlock) -> list[GesamtCell]:
    cells: list[GesamtCell] = []
    for idx, week in enumerate(weeks):
        used = sum(p.cells[idx].value for p in block.projects)
        absence = block.absence.cells[idx].value if block.absence.cells else 0.0
        internal = block.internal.cells[idx].value if block.internal.cells else 0.0
        work = scaled_work_days(week, block.workload_percent)
        result = UtilizationService.compute_employee_gesamt(
            used_days=used,
            absence_days=absence,
            internal_days=internal,
            work_days=work,
        )
        cells.append(
            GesamtCell(
                week_key=week.key,
                value=result.free_days,
                bucket=result.bucket,
                state=gesamt_state(result.free_days),
                has_absence=result.has_absence,
                breakdown=gesamt_breakdown(
                    work, used, internal, absence, result.free_days
                ),
            )
        )
    return cells


def compute_heat(weeks: list[WeekColumn], block: EmployeeBlock) -> list[HeatCell]:
    cells: list[HeatCell] = []
    for idx, week in enumerate(weeks):
        used = sum(p.cells[idx].value for p in block.projects)
        absence = block.absence.cells[idx].value if block.absence.cells else 0.0
        internal = block.internal.cells[idx].value if block.internal.cells else 0.0
        result = UtilizationService.compute_employee_heat(
            used_days=used,
            absence_days=absence,
            internal_days=internal,
            work_days=scaled_work_days(week, block.workload_percent),
        )
        cells.append(
            HeatCell(
                week_key=week.key,
                percent=result.percent,
                is_absent=result.is_absent,
                bucket=result.bucket,
            )
        )
    return cells


def compute_project_gesamt(
    weeks: list[WeekColumn], block: ProjectBlock
) -> list[ProjectGesamtCell]:
    cells: list[ProjectGesamtCell] = []
    for idx, week in enumerate(weeks):
        allocated = sum(
            e.cells[idx].value for e in block.employees if idx < len(e.cells)
        )
        _, bucket = UtilizationService.compute_project_gesamt(allocated)
        cells.append(
            ProjectGesamtCell(week_key=week.key, allocated=allocated, bucket=bucket)
        )
    return cells


def compute_project_heat(
    weeks: list[WeekColumn], block: ProjectBlock
) -> list[HeatCell]:
    cells: list[HeatCell] = []
    n = len(block.employees)
    for idx, week in enumerate(weeks):
        allocated = sum(
            e.cells[idx].value for e in block.employees if idx < len(e.cells)
        )
        result = UtilizationService.compute_project_heat(
            allocated_days=allocated,
            num_employees=n,
            work_days=week.work_days,
        )
        cells.append(
            HeatCell(
                week_key=week.key,
                percent=result.percent,
                is_absent=False,
                bucket=result.bucket,
            )
        )
    return cells


def employee_summary(block: EmployeeBlock, from_key: str) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Planned and available person-days from ``from_key`` onward.
"""Shared utilization calculation service.

Single source of truth for all capacity and utilization computations.
Both the planning grid heatmap and the dashboard KPI cards use this service
so that numbers always match.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, timedelta

WORK_DAYS_PER_WEEK: int = 5
HOURS_PER_DAY: float = 8.0
HEAT_LOW: int = 70
HEAT_MID: int = 85
HEAT_HIGH: int = 100
PROJECT_ALLOC_MID: float = 2.0
PROJECT_ALLOC_HIGH: float = 4.0
FREE_DAYS_PRECISION: int = 2


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data types
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AbsencePeriod:
    """Minimal absence representation for utilization calculation."""

    start_date: date
    end_date: date


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class HeatResult:
    """Utilization result for a single employee in a single week."""

    percent: int
    bucket: str
    is_absent: bool
    available_days: float
    used_days: float


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GesamtResult:
    """Free-days result for a single employee in a single week."""

    free_days: float
    bucket: str
    has_absence: bool


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ProjectHeatResult:
    """Utilization result for a single project in a single week."""

    percent: int
        if free_days >= -1.0:
            return "tight"
        return "over"

    @staticmethod
    def project_heat_bucket(allocated: float) -> str:
        """Classify project allocation into a bucket."""
        if allocated <= 0:
            return "low"
        if allocated <= PROJECT_ALLOC_MID:
            return "mid"
        if allocated <= PROJECT_ALLOC_HIGH:
            return "high"
        return "over"

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Holiday + workload helpers (shared work-days computation)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    @staticmethod
    def holidays_in_week(
        holiday_dates: set[date] | frozenset[date] | None,
        week_start: date,
    ) -> int:
        """Count Mon-Fri public holidays falling within the week."""
        if not holiday_dates:
            return 0
        count = 0
        for offset in range(WORK_DAYS_PER_WEEK):
            day = week_start + timedelta(days=offset)
            if day in holiday_dates:
                count += 1
        return count

    @staticmethod
    def apply_workload(work_days: float, workload_percent: int) -> float:
        """Scale a baseline work-day count by employee workload percentage."""
        wp = max(0, int(workload_percent))
        return max(0.0, work_days * wp / 100.0)

    @classmethod
    def work_days_for_week(
        cls,
        week_start: date,
        holiday_dates: set[date] | frozenset[date] | None,
        workload_percent: int = 100,
        base_work_days: float = float(WORK_DAYS_PER_WEEK),
    ) -> float:
        """Return effective work days for one employee in one week.

        Single source of truth for capacity calculations: subtracts public
        holidays from the base week, then scales by employee workload.
        """
        holidays = cls.holidays_in_week(holiday_dates, week_start)
        return cls.apply_workload(base_work_days - holidays, workload_percent)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Absence helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    @staticmethod
    def absence_days_in_week(
        absences: list[AbsencePeriod] | tuple[AbsencePeriod, ...],
        week_start: date,
    ) -> float:
        """Count Mon-Fri days of a week covered by at least one absence.

        Overlapping absence periods are merged, so a day is counted once.
        """
        workdays = [week_start + timedelta(days=i) for i in range(WORK_DAYS_PER_WEEK)]
        covered = {
            day
            for a in absences
            for day in workdays
            if day.weekday() < WORK_DAYS_PER_WEEK and a.start_date <= day <= a.end_date
        }
        return float(len(covered))

    @staticmethod
    def cap_internal_days(
        internal_hours: int,
        absence_days: float,
        work_days: float = 5.0,
    ) -> float:
        """Cap internal days so they don't exceed remaining capacity."""
        internal_days = internal_hours / HOURS_PER_DAY
        return max(0.0, min(internal_days, work_days - absence_days))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Employee-level computations (per week)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    @classmethod
    def compute_employee_heat(
        cls,
        used_days: float,
        absence_days: float,
        internal_days: float,
        work_days: float = 5.0,
    ) -> HeatResult:
        """Compute heatmap percent for one employee in one week.

        This is the canonical formula used by the planning grid heatmap.
        Parameters use pre-computed values (internal already capped).
        """
        fully_absent = absence_days >= float(WORK_DAYS_PER_WEEK)
        available = max(0.0, work_days - internal_days - absence_days)

        if fully_absent:
            denom = work_days - internal_days
            pct = round((used_days / denom) * 100) if denom > 0 else 0
            bucket = "absent"
        elif available > 0:
            pct = round((used_days / available) * 100)
            bucket = cls.heat_bucket(pct)
        else:
            pct = 0
            bucket = "low"

        return HeatResult(
            percent=pct,
            bucket=bucket,
            is_absent=fully_absent,
            available_days=available,
            used_days=used_days,
        )

    @classmethod
    def compute_employee_gesamt(
        cls,
        used_days: float,
        absence_days: float,
        internal_days: float,
        work_days: float = 5.0,
    ) -> GesamtResult:
        """Compute free days for one employee in one week."""
        has_absence = absence_days > 0

def app_page(

    sidebar: rx.Component,
    *,
    toolbar: rx.Component | None = None,
    scope: rx.Component | None = None,
    padded: bool = True,
    admin_only: bool = False,
    on_load: EventType[()] | Sequence[Any] | None = None,
) -> Callable[[Callable[[], rx.Component]], rx.Component]:
    """Authenticated page in the app shell.

    Registers the route through appkit's ``authenticated_page`` (session
    monitor, admin gate, loading state) with our window as template.
    """
    handlers = desktop_handlers(on_load)

    def template(content: rx.Component) -> rx.Component:
        window = app_layout(sidebar, toolbar, content, scope=scope, padded=padded)
        return rx.fragment(splash(), window) if is_desktop() else window

    return authenticated_page(
        route=route,
        title=title,
        template=template,
        admin_only=admin_only,
        on_load=cast("Any", handlers),
    )

"""Heatmap view: tones, row summaries, team row, KPIs and the detail panel."""

from datetime import date
from unittest.mock import patch

import pytest
from alloq_commons.models.employee import Employee
from alloq_project.components.planning_heatmap import planning_heatmap
from alloq_project.services.planning_builders import (
    build_employee_meta,
    build_weeks,
    cell_key,
)
from alloq_project.services.planning_heatmap import (
    de_days,
    heat_tone,
    week_range,
)
from alloq_project.states.planning_grid_state import PlanningStore


@pytest.fixture
def planning() -> PlanningStore:
    """Ada 3 PT (60 %), Ben 5 PT (100 %), Cora 6 PT (120 %) from week 1 on."""
    state = PlanningStore()
    with patch(
        "alloq_project.services.planning_builders.anchor_date",
        return_value=date(2026, 9, 28),
    ):
        state.weeks, state.month_spans = build_weeks(3)
    state.current_week = state.weeks[1].key
    state.view_mode = "Heatmap"
    state.available_employees = [
        Employee(id=1, first_name="Ada", last_name="Zeh", internal_hours=0),
        Employee(id=2, first_name="Ben", last_name="Abt", internal_hours=0),
        Employee(id=3, first_name="Cora", last_name="Mohr", internal_hours=0),
    ]
    state.employee_meta, state.absence_days = build_employee_meta(
        state.available_employees, state._week_keys()
    )
    state.employee_meta = [
        {**employee, "project_ids": ["proj-1"]} for employee in state.employee_meta
    ]
    state.project_meta = [
        {
            "id": "proj-1",
            "real_id": 1,
            "code": "A",
            "name": "Alpha",
            "color": "#123456",
            "employee_ids": ["emp-1", "emp-2", "emp-3"],
        }
    ]
    state.cells = {
        cell_key(f"emp-{emp_id}", "A", week.key): days
        for emp_id, days in [(1, 3.0), (2, 5.0), (3, 6.0)]
        for week in state.weeks[1:]
    }
    state.saved_cells = dict(state.cells)
    return state


def _set_absence(state: PlanningStore, emp_id: str, idx: int, days: float) -> None:
    absence = dict(state.absence_days)
    row = list(absence[emp_id])
    row[idx] = days
    absence[emp_id] = row
    state.absence_days = absence


class TestHeatTone:
    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        ("percent", "tone"),
        [
            (0, "zero"),
            (1, "low"),
            (69, "low"),
            (70, "mid"),
            (84, "mid"),
            (85, "high"),
            (100, "high"),
            (101, "over"),
            (150, "over"),
            (151, "critical"),
        ],
    )
    def test_thresholds(self, percent: int, tone: str) -> None:
        assert heat_tone(percent, is_absent=False) == tone

    def test_absence_wins(self) -> None:
        assert heat_tone(120, is_absent=True) == "absent"


class TestFormatting:
    def test_week_range_within_month(self) -> None:
        assert week_range("2026_10_19") == "19.–23. Okt 2026"

    def test_week_range_across_months(self) -> None:
        assert week_range("2026_12_28") == "28. Dez – 1. Jan 2027"

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        ("value", "text"), [(6.0, "6"), (14.3, "14,3"), (0.0, "0"), (2.25, "2,2")]
    )
    def test_de_days(self, value: float, text: str) -> None:
        assert de_days(value) == text


class TestHeatCells:
    def test_cells_carry_booked_capacity_and_absence(
        self, planning: PlanningStore
    ) -> None:
        _set_absence(planning, "emp-1", 3, 2.0)
        ada = next(e for e in planning.employees if e.id == "emp-1")
        cell = ada.heat[3]
        assert cell.booked_days == 3.0
        assert cell.capacity_days == 3.0
        assert cell.absence_days == 2.0
        assert cell.percent == 100

    def test_rows_add_tone_and_hint(self, planning: PlanningStore) -> None:
        _set_absence(planning, "emp-1", 3, 2.0)
        ada = next(r for r in planning.heat_rows if r.id == "emp-1")
        week_no = planning.weeks[3].week_no
        assert ada.cells[0].tone == "zero"
        assert ada.cells[1].tone == "low"
        assert ada.cells[3].tone == "high"
        assert ada.cells[3].hint == (
            f"KW {week_no}: 100 %, 3 von 3 PT gebucht, 2 Tage abwesend"
        )

    def test_full_absence_hint(self, planning: PlanningStore) -> None:
        _set_absence(planning, "emp-1", 2, 5.0)
        ada = next(r for r in planning.heat_rows if r.id == "emp-1")
        assert ada.cells[2].tone == "absent"
        assert ada.cells[2].hint == f"KW {planning.weeks[2].week_no}: abwesend"


class TestHeatRows:
    def test_sorted_by_last_name_by_default(self, planning: PlanningStore) -> None:
        assert [r.name for r in planning.heat_rows] == [
            "Ben Abt",
            "Cora Mohr",
            "Ada Zeh",
        ]

    def test_average_counts_from_current_week(self, planning: PlanningStore) -> None:
        by_id = {r.id: r for r in planning.heat_rows}
        assert by_id["emp-1"].avg_percent == 60
        assert by_id["emp-1"].avg_tone == "low"
        assert by_id["emp-3"].avg_percent == 120
        assert by_id["emp-3"].avg_tone == "over"

    def test_average_skips_absent_weeks(self, planning: PlanningStore) -> None:
        _set_absence(planning, "emp-3", 2, 5.0)
        cora = next(r for r in planning.heat_rows if r.id == "emp-3")
        assert cora.avg_percent == 120

    def test_free_from(self, planning: PlanningStore) -> None:
        planning.cells = {
            **planning.cells,
            **{cell_key("emp-2", "A", w.key): 0.0 for w in planning.weeks[5:]},
        }
        by_id = {r.id: r for r in planning.heat_rows}
        assert (by_id["emp-1"].free_from, by_id["emp-1"].free_state) == (
            "sofort",
            "now",
        )
        assert (by_id["emp-2"].free_from, by_id["emp-2"].free_state) == (
            f"KW {planning.weeks[5].week_no}",
            "later",
        )
        assert (by_id["emp-3"].free_from, by_id["emp-3"].free_state) == (
            "—",
            "none",
        )

    def test_sort_by_average(self, planning: PlanningStore) -> None:
        planning.set_heat_sort("avg")
        assert [r.id for r in planning.heat_rows] == ["emp-3", "emp-2", "emp-1"]

    def test_sort_by_free_from(self, planning: PlanningStore) -> None:
        planning.cells = {
            **planning.cells,
            **{cell_key("emp-3", "A", w.key): 0.0 for w in planning.weeks[4:]},
        }
        planning.set_heat_sort("free")
        assert [r.id for r in planning.heat_rows] == ["emp-1", "emp-3", "emp-2"]

    def test_unknown_sort_is_ignored(self, planning: PlanningStore) -> None:
        planning.set_heat_sort("bogus")
        assert planning.heat_sort == "name"

    def test_empty_outside_heatmap(self, planning: PlanningStore) -> None:
        planning.view_mode = "Grid"
        assert planning.heat_rows == []
        assert planning.heat_team == []


class TestTeamRow:
    def test_weighted_by_capacity(self, planning: PlanningStore) -> None:
        team = planning.heat_team
        assert len(team) == len(planning.weeks)
        assert team[0].percent == 0
        assert team[0].tone == "zero"
        assert team[0].free_days == 15.0
        # (3 + 5 + 6) / 15 PT = 93 %; only Ada has 2 PT left.
        assert team[1].percent == 93
        assert team[1].tone == "high"
        assert team[1].free_days == 2.0
        assert team[1].free_label == "2"

    def test_fully_absent_people_add_no_capacity(
        self, planning: PlanningStore
    ) -> None:
        for emp_id in ("emp-1", "emp-2", "emp-3"):
            _set_absence(planning, emp_id, 2, 5.0)
        assert planning.heat_team[2].has_capacity is False
        assert planning.heat_team[2].tone == "absent"


class TestKpis:
    def test_current_week_figures(self, planning: PlanningStore) -> None:
        kpis = planning.heat_kpis
        assert kpis.week_no == planning.weeks[1].week_no
        assert kpis.over_count == 1
        assert kpis.over_names == "Cora Mohr"
        assert kpis.free_label == "2"
        assert kpis.free_people == 1
        assert kpis.team_percent == 93
        assert kpis.next_absence == "Keine geplant"

    def test_next_absence(self, planning: PlanningStore) -> None:
        _set_absence(planning, "emp-2", 4, 5.0)
        _set_absence(planning, "emp-3", 4, 5.0)
        kpis = planning.heat_kpis
        assert kpis.next_absence == f"KW {planning.weeks[4].week_no}"
        assert kpis.next_absence_names == "Ben Abt, Cora Mohr"


class TestDetail:
    def test_closed_by_default(self, planning: PlanningStore) -> None:
        assert planning.has_heat_detail is False

    def test_select_shows_overbooked_week(self, planning: PlanningStore) -> None:
        week = planning.weeks[1]
        planning.select_heat_cell("emp-3", week.key)
        assert planning.has_heat_detail is True
        detail = planning.heat_detail
        assert detail.name == "Cora Mohr"
        assert detail.week_no == week.week_no
        assert detail.date_range == week_range(week.key)
        assert detail.percent == 120
        assert detail.tone == "over"
        assert detail.summary == "6 PT gebucht bei 5 PT Kapazität, 1 PT zu viel."
        assert detail.bar_normal == pytest.approx(83.33, abs=0.01)
        assert detail.bar_over == pytest.approx(16.67, abs=0.01)
        assert [(a.name, a.days_label, a.color) for a in detail.assignments] == [
            ("Alpha", "6 PT", "#123456")
        ]

    def test_free_and_absent_summaries(self, planning: PlanningStore) -> None:
        planning.select_heat_cell("emp-1", planning.weeks[0].key)
        assert planning.heat_detail.summary == "Keine Zuweisung, 5 PT frei."
        assert planning.heat_detail.assignments == []

        assert planning.heat_detail.summary == "3 von 5 PT gebucht, 2 PT frei."
        _set_absence(planning, "emp-1", 2, 5.0)
        planning.select_heat_cell("emp-1", planning.weeks[2].key)
        assert planning.heat_detail.summary == "Die ganze Woche abwesend."

    def test_partial_absence_is_mentioned(self, planning: PlanningStore) -> None:
        _set_absence(planning, "emp-1", 3, 2.0)

        planning.select_heat_cell("emp-1", key)

    def test_close(self, planning: PlanningStore) -> None:
        planning.select_heat_cell("emp-1", planning.weeks[1].key)

    def test_filtered_out_employee_closes_panel(self, planning: PlanningStore) -> None:

"""Heatmap styles, the KPI and legend bar, and the cell detail panel."""

from __future__ import annotations

import reflex as rx
from alloq_commons import theme
from alloq_project.states.planning_grid_state import PlanningStore
from alloq_project.states.planning_models import HeatAssignment
from reflex.vars import ObjectVar

import appkit_mantine as mn

TONES = ("zero", "low", "mid", "high", "over", "critical")
STRONG_TONES = {"high": 700, "over": 800, "critical": 800}

_TONE_CSS = "".join(
    f".aq-heat-{tone}{{background-color:{theme.token(f'heat-{tone}')};"
    f"color:{theme.token(f'heat-{tone}-text')};"
    f"font-weight:{STRONG_TONES.get(tone, 600 if tone != 'zero' else 400)};}}"
    for tone in TONES
)

HEATMAP_CSS = (
    ".aq-heat-cell{all:unset;box-sizing:border-box;width:100%;height:26px;"
    "border-radius:5px;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;"
    "font-size:12px;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;cursor:pointer;"
    "position:relative;transition:filter 120ms,box-shadow 120ms;}"
    ".aq-heat-cell:hover{filter:brightness(1.08);}"
    ".aq-heat-cell:focus-visible,.aq-heat-cell[data-selected=true]"
    f"{{box-shadow:0 0 0 2px {theme.SURFACE},0 0 0 4px {theme.TEXT};z-index:1;}}"
    ".aq-heat-cell[data-partial=true]::after{content:'';position:absolute;top:0;"
    f"right:0;border-left:8px solid transparent;border-top:8px solid "
    f"{theme.TEXT_MUTED};border-top-right-radius:5px;}}"
    ".aq-heat-static{cursor:default;height:22px;font-size:11.5px;}"
    ".aq-heat-static:hover{filter:none;}"
    + _TONE_CSS
    + ".aq-heat-absent{background:repeating-linear-gradient(45deg,transparent 0 4px,"
    f"{theme.token('heat-stripe')} 4px 8px);color:{theme.TEXT_MUTED};}}"
    ".aq-heat-pill{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;"
    "min-width:36px;height:20px;padding:0 6px;border-radius:10px;font-size:11.5px;"
    "font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;box-sizing:border-box;}"
    ".aq-heat-swatch{width:16px;height:10px;border-radius:3px;display:inline-block;"
    "position:relative;}"
    f".aq-heat-row:hover>*,.aq-heat-row[data-selected=true]>*"
    f"{{background-color:{theme.HOVER};}}"
    f".aq-heat-now{{background-image:linear-gradient({theme.token('now')},"
    f"{theme.token('now')});}}"
    ".aq-heat-th{all:unset;box-sizing:border-box;display:flex;align-items:center;"
    f"gap:4px;padding:0 10px;height:30px;font-size:11px;font-weight:600;"
    f"color:{theme.TEXT_MUTED};cursor:pointer;}}"
    f".aq-heat-th[data-active=true]{{color:{theme.TEXT};}}"
    ".aq-heat-th svg{opacity:0;}.aq-heat-th[data-active=true] svg{opacity:1;}"
    f".aq-heat-th:focus-visible{{outline:2px solid {theme.ACCENT};outline-offset:-2px;}}"
)

CAPS_LABEL = {
    "fontSize": "10.5px",
    "fontWeight": "600",
    "letterSpacing": "0.06em",
    "textTransform": "uppercase",
    "color": theme.TEXT_MUTED,
    "whiteSpace": "nowrap",
}


def tone_class(base: str, tone: rx.Var[str]) -> rx.Var[str]:
    """``"<base> aq-heat-<tone>"`` for a cell or pill."""
    return base + " aq-heat-" + tone


# ---------------------------- KPI and legend bar ----------------------------


def _kpi(
    label: rx.Var[str] | str,
    value: rx.Var[str] | str,
    detail: rx.Var[str] | str,
    *,
    value_color: str = theme.TEXT,
) -> rx.Component:
    return mn.stack(
        mn.text(label, style=CAPS_LABEL),
        mn.group(
            mn.text(value, size="md", fw="700", c=value_color, style=theme.NUMERIC),
            mn.text(
                detail,
                size="xs",
                c=theme.TEXT_MUTED,
                truncate="end",
                style={"maxWidth": "220px"},
            ),
            gap=6,
            wrap="nowrap",
            align="baseline",
        ),
        gap=0,
    )


def _legend_item(tone: str, label: str) -> rx.Component:
    return mn.group(

content.text:
I built the new heatmap without changing the page header or the filters. All 700 tests pass, along with lint and typecheck. I couldn't look at it in a browser, though: the built-in browser refused localhost, the Playwright browser was in use by another session, and the third browser was sent to Microsoft sign-in, where I stopped.

**Colors are blue, not teal.** The app now uses the theme in `alloq_commons/theme.py` (blue accent). The Alloq design system I used for the mockup still has the old teal look. So I kept the design's logic and used the app's colors:
- **0 to 100 %:** light to dark blue, getting stronger the more is booked.
- **Overbooked:** orange for 101 to 150 %, dark red above 150 %.
- **Absent:** striped cell. A small corner notch marks a partial absence.

The colors are new tokens in `theme.py`, for both light and dark mode.

**Details panel, as you asked:**
- Clicking a cell opens a single-row panel pinned to the bottom of the window. The table above it shrinks and scrolls, so the panel never covers anything.
- The panel shows the name, week and dates, the percentage, a short summary ("6 PT gebucht bei 5 PT Kapazität, 1 PT zu viel."), a capacity bar, and the projects booked that week.
- "Im Raster bearbeiten" opens that person in the Team grid. Note that this sets the Mitarbeiter filter to that person.
- Close it with the X or by clicking the same cell again.

**Also from the design:**
- A strip at the top with four numbers (overbooked this week, free PT this week, team utilization from this week on, next absence) and the color legend.
- Sortable columns "Ø %" (average from the current week on) and "Frei ab" (first week with at least 30 % free capacity).
- The current week is marked with a blue pill in the header and a tinted column.
- The footer now shows team utilization weighted by capacity, plus a new "PT frei" row. It replaces the old plain average row (`avg_heat`), and I updated the three tests that used it.

**Files:**
- The logic is in [planning_heatmap.py](components/alloq-project/src/alloq_project/services/planning_heatmap.py) (service) and [planning_heatmap_mixin.py](components/alloq-project/src/alloq_project/states/planning_heatmap_mixin.py). It is a mixin, so `PlanningStore` got smaller.
- The view is in [planning_heatmap.py](components/alloq-project/src/alloq_project/components/planning_heatmap.py) and [planning_heatmap_parts.py](components/alloq-project/src/alloq_project/components/planning_heatmap_parts.py).
- New tests are in [test_planning_heatmap.py](components/alloq-project/tests/test_planning_heatmap.py), with 98 % coverage of the new logic.

**Things to know:**
- Another session is changing `planning_models.py` and `planning_grid_state.py` for the Abwesenheiten view at the same time, so both sets of changes are in those files. Its `planning_gantt.py` still has one lint error.
- `planning_grid_state.py` is at 1010 lines, still over the 1000-line limit even after removing `avg_heat`.
- The heatmap always uses the compact row height. The density switch is in the page header, which I left alone.

- **Numbers at the top removed.** Only the legend is left above the table. I also deleted the code behind those numbers (the state, the calculation and their tests), since nothing uses it any more.

content.text:
The Heatmap view is gone. The planning page now has three views: Team, Projekte and Abwesenheiten. All 650 remaining tests pass, and lint is clean. I haven't checked it in a browser.

**Removed:**
- The view itself: its two component files, its state, its helper module and its test file.
- The "Heatmap" button in the view switch and the Heatmap entry in the planning page.
- The heatmap-only parts of the planning state, including the `employees` list, which only that view used. [planning_grid_state.py](components/alloq-project/src/alloq_project/states/planning_grid_state.py) is now 993 lines, back under the 1000-line limit.
- The heatmap data models and the `heat` field on employee and project rows.
- The functions that calculated that data. Nothing else used `compute_project_heat` either; the project view never showed it.
- The heatmap colors I had added to `theme.py`, and their test.
- The `#planning-heatmap-root` CSS rule and the Heatmap mention in the README.
- Heatmap tests in four existing test files. One test that switched to "Heatmap" now uses "Abwesenheiten".

**Kept on purpose:**
- The shared utilization calculations in `alloq_commons/services/utilization.py`. The names say "heat", but the dashboard and the Team overview still use them to calculate utilization.
- `assets/css/alloq-theme.org.css` still names the heatmap. Nothing loads that file; it looks like an old copy of the theme, so I didn't touch it.
- `doc/plans/macos-app-rahmen.md` still lists Heatmap as a view. It's a planning document, not code.

**Not from this change:** the type checker still reports 5 errors in the Abwesenheiten view code that the other session is working on.

Nothing is committed.
